title: Autoencoders & VAEs
interviewAnswer: A standard autoencoder learns a compressed code for reconstruction. A VAE regularizes the latent distribution and samples from it, enabling generation but introducing a reconstruction–regularization trade-off.
why: VAEs introduce probabilistic latent-variable models, reconstruction–regularization trade-offs and the reparameterization trick.
intuition: An encoder predicts a distribution over latent codes rather than one fixed code. Sample a latent, decode it, and regularize the latent distribution so nearby codes form a usable generative space.
deepDive: The VAE maximizes an evidence lower bound: expected reconstruction log-likelihood minus KL divergence between approximate posterior q(z|x) and prior p(z). Reparameterization z=μ+σ⊙ε makes sampling differentiable with respect to μ/σ. Strong KL pressure can cause posterior collapse; weak pressure yields poor prior sampling. Output likelihood determines the reconstruction term.
math:
ELBO = E_{q(z|x)}[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z|x)||p(z))
z=μ+σ⊙ε, ε~N(0,I)
workedExample: A VAE can interpolate smoothly between latent codes and sample from a known prior, but reconstructions may be blurrier than adversarial/perceptual models.
code:
mu, logvar = encoder(x)
std=(0.5*logvar).exp(); z=mu+std*torch.randn_like(std)
xhat=decoder(z)
commonMistakes: Forgetting the KL term/why it exists.
Using MSE reconstruction blindly without considering data likelihood.
production: VAEs provide compact latent representations and uncertainty-friendly generation, but validate latent stability and reconstruction quality under domain shift.
